title: Machinery Monitoring Engineer
jobDescription:
About the Position The Machinery Monitoring Engineer is part of Reliability and Integrity organization within Chevron’s ENGINE Center. This role provides remote monitoring, diagnostics, and development of new solutions for critical rotating equipment across Chevron's North America deepwater operating assets. Monitoring activities include the subsea pump predictive analytics development and monitoring, review of oil samples and analysis, major rotating equipment optimization and performance analysis reviews, history brief assistance after major repairs while providing insights to business unit customers through weekly or bi-weekly reporting and meetings. Key responsibilities Support the expansion and deployment of predictive analytics and advanced diagnostic tools for machinery performance evaluation and early warning detection, with a particular focus on subsea pump monitoring and performance analysis. Subsea equipment monitoring includes subsea pumps and support systems, including HPUs and control systems. This requires interfacing with the Deepwater Support Center and the Subsea Operations Team. Identifying and reporting subsea equipment anomalies promptly to the subsea operations team. Maintaining and updating the equipment performance monitoring tool and integrating any new subsea pump systems installed into the tool. Engage closely with deepwater engineering and operations teams to support equipment troubleshooting, identify long-term performance trends, and detect early signs of degradation or abnormal operation. Perform equipment health assessments and provide data-driven optimization and reliability improvement recommendations. Review, and analyse lubricating oil sample reports, assess machinery condition, develop trend analyses, and proactively notify the region of abnormal conditions or emerging risks. Support data collection, analysis, and reporting for benchmarking critical rotating equipment reliability, availability, and efficiency metrics across the region. Assist in the development of equipment history briefs following major maintenance or repair activities, ensuring lessons learned and performance impacts are clearly documented. title: Earth Scientist, Asset Business Delivery
jobDescription: The Chevron Engineering and Innovation Excellence Center (ENGINE) in Bengaluru India bring s together the resources and expertise of the Chevron global network with talent in India to enhance agility and technological innovation to optimize solutions for the world’s current and future energy challenges. As one of the leading energy providers worldwide, Chevron is involved in the production of crude oil and natural gas, manufacturing of transportation fuels, lubricants, petrochemicals, and additives, and the development of enabling technologies. Chevron's vision is to be the global energy company most admired for its people, partnerships, and performance. With a clear purpose to develop affordable, reliable, ever-cleaner energy that enables human progress, we believe human ingenuity has the power to solve any challenge and overcome any obstacle. Meeting the world’s growing energy needs requires the pursuit of innovations and advancements that deliver a better future for all. About the position : The Asset Business Delivery Earth Scientist is responsible and accountable for delivering technical support to business segments to enable asset growth through brownfield and post-initial investment decision greenfield opportunities. The successful candidate should have broad experience across geology and geophysics disciplines and will deliver subsurface characterization that may include seismic interpretation, well log and surveillance data integration, earth modeling, resource maturation, well maturation, and technology deployment. Chevron ENGINE supports global operations, and work hours are aligned to business needs. Standard working hours are 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM or 1:30 PM to 10:30 PM, Monday to Friday. These may evolve based on operational or business requirements. Key Responsibilities Minimum Experience required: 5 -15 years Expertise in integrated subsurface characterization, including demonstrated knowledge of seismic interpretation, mapping, log interpretation, earth modelling, stratigraphy, structural geology, deepwater depositional environment, static model building, and volumetric assessment. Ability to utilize multiple datasets (e.g., logs, pressure, geochem, rock quality, etc.) for integrated interpretation. Proficient in Petrel and able to utilize/update static models, collaborate with simulation engineers, and support new model construction. Experience utilizing workflows and tools for generating new asset development opportunities to mature resources to reserves to production, assessing/mitigating risk, and advancing capital projects. Skill collaborating and communicating with technical peers, cross-disciplinary teams, and other stakeholders. Able to serve as mentor and adopt/deploy relevant technology. Domain knowledge relevant to the energy sector and working knowledge of Oil and Gas value chain (e.g., upstream, midstream, or downstream). Candidates should have a proven ability to develop integrated interpretations across Geological, Geophysical and Petrophysical data sets and deliver high-quality reservoir management work products and project deliverables. Fluency in Petrel or similar software is required. Preferred Qualifications Earth modeling experience and skills is a bonus. Experience with digital/data projects and/or agile project management is a plus. A breadth of upstream experience would be beneficial including: reservoir management, progression of major capital projects, new field start-up, base business, functional excellence. DW and gas field experience not required, but desirable.
